Claims Management & Claim Scrubbing

Catching Errors Before the Payer Does

Claims management covers everything that happens to a claim from the moment it is created to the moment it is fully adjudicated: validation, scrubbing, transmission, status tracking, and correction if anything comes back. Get any one of those steps wrong and a clean claim becomes a rejected one, adding days or weeks to payment.

Claim scrubbing is the safeguard that catches problems before submission: coding edits, payer-specific formatting rules, missing modifiers and eligibility mismatches are all checked automatically, so what reaches the payer is already clean. In-house billing tools built with this discipline routinely push first-time claim acceptance rates above 98%.

PMEX runs the same scrubbing discipline on every claim your practice generates, then tracks each one through submission, adjudication and, if necessary, correction and resubmission, all visible in the PMEX dashboard.

Claim Scrubbing & Submission

From Charge to Clean Claim in Four Checks

A claim only earns the label clean once it passes each of these checks. Skipping any one of them is how rejections happen.

Coding Validation

ICD-10, CPT and HCPCS codes checked for accuracy and specificity.

Payer Edit Checks

Claim tested against the specific payer's formatting and coverage rules.

Modifier & Eligibility Check

Required modifiers and current eligibility confirmed before submission.

Final Scrub & Transmit

Claim transmitted electronically through the clearinghouse and tracked to receipt.

Rejections vs Denials

Two Different Problems, Two Different Fixes

Practices often treat these the same way, which slows both down. PMEX handles them as separate workflows.

Claim Rejection

A rejection happens before adjudication, usually from a formatting or eligibility error caught by the clearinghouse or payer edits. Rejections never reach medical review, so they are corrected and resubmitted quickly, typically within days.

Claim Denial

A denial happens after the payer reviews the claim and refuses payment, often for medical necessity, coverage or documentation reasons. Denials require an appeal or corrected claim, and are handled through PMEX's dedicated denial management process.
